evidence: In a series of Fe3O4 nanotube arrays of varying wall thickness dw (all other geometric parameters being kept constant), investigated by superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) magnetometry, we observed a significant dependence of the coercivity and remanence on the geometry. In particular, the coercive field Hc can be tuned between 0 and 800 Oe (0 and 80 mT) approximately by properly adjusting dw. Most curiously, the dependence of Hc on dw is not monotonic—Hc reaches its maximum at dw ≈13 nm and then decreases for further increases in the wall thickness (Fig. 6(b)).
